note.text:
A form asks for information on lines or in boxes. Read each label before you write.
• Surname (family name) and first name. “In BLOCK LETTERS” means in capital letters: EBAI.
• Date of birth: day, month, year: 14/05/2014 or 14 May 2014.
• Place of birth, address, class, phone number.
• Signature: your own way of writing your name, always the same.
Write clearly, do not leave a line empty (write “None” if it does not apply), and check everything before you sign.
An invitation tells: who is invited, what the event is, when (day and time), where, and how to reply. Example: “Dear Mih, please come to my birthday party on Saturday at three o'clock at our house. Please reply by Thursday. Your friend, Bih.”

worked_example.problem: {first} {sur} fills in the form for a library card. The form asks for: Surname (in BLOCK LETTERS), First name, Date of birth (dd/mm/yyyy), Place of birth. She was born in {place} on {d} {monthName(m)} {y}.
steps: Date of birth (dd/mm/yyyy): day first, then month, then year: {ddmmyyyy(d, m, y)}

paper_task.prompt: In your exercise book, copy this form and fill it in for yourself: Surname (in BLOCK LETTERS) · First name · Date of birth (dd/mm/yyyy) · Place of birth · Class · Name of parent or guardian · Signature. Then write a short invitation to a friend for a party or a match.
model: Dear Akwen, please come to my birthday party on Saturday at three o'clock at our house in Mamfe. Please reply by Thursday. Your friend, {first}.
checklist: My surname is in BLOCK LETTERS.
My date of birth is day, then month, then year.
My signature is the way I always sign.
My invitation says who, what, when and where.
My invitation asks my friend to reply.
I checked my capital letters and spelling.
